title: Ideal of a base-changed closed subscheme on affine opens
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $\mathcal I_Y\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be the ideal sheaf of the projection $Z\times_XY\to Y$ from the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $U\subseteq X$ and $V\subseteq Y$ are affine opens with $V\subseteq g^{-1}(U)$, and $g^\sharp_{U,V}:\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_Y(V)$ is the ring map induced by $g$ (in Lean, $g.appLE\,U\,V$), then $\mathcal I_Y(V)$ is the ideal of $\mathcal O_Y(V)$ generated by $g^\sharp_{U,V}(\mathcal I(U))$.

proof.text: Use the attached, sorry-free source implementation Scheme.IdealSheafData.ideal_comap_appLE (WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Affine.lean, lines 95-110). Its independent proof first treats affine schemes: the Galois connection between ideal-sheaf comap and map, and the affine identification of map with ring-theoretic Ideal.comap, identify comap with Ideal.map. The two inequalities follow from the unit and counit of those Galois connections. Restrict J to the target affine open and J.comap f to the source affine open; comap_comp and resLE_comp_ι identify these restrictions with comap along f.resLE. Transport the affine formula through the two top-section isomorphisms. Ideal.map_map and resLE_app_top then give exactly extension along f.appLE. This implementation does not call modulePullbackIdealQuotient and does not use its planned proof.
